LONG-TERM MODELING
To determine the long-term or annual average ground level concentrations the following equation was used (Turner, 1970).
\chi(x,\theta) = \sum_{SN} \left\{ \frac{2Qf(\theta,S,N)}{\sqrt{2\pi} \sigma_{ZS} \overline{U}_{n} \frac{2\pi x}{16}} \exp \left[ \frac{-1}{2} \frac{H_{u}}{\sigma_{ZS}}^{2} \right] \right\} 5.3
where:
f(\theta,S,N)
 = the frequency during the period of interest that the wind is from the direction 
\theta
, for the stability condition, S, and wind speed class N.
The vertical dispersion parameter evaluated at the distance x for the stability condition S.
\overline{U}_{n}
 = the representative wind speed for class N.
H_{u}
 = the effective height of release for the wind speed 
\overline{U}_{n}
.
x = the distance downwind.
Q = the emission rate in micrograms per second.
SHORT-TERM MODELING
Surface concentrations of effluents from the hypothetical SNG facility may occur on a short-term basis (3-hour, 24-hour) as a result of the three different meteorological patterns; 1) limited mixing, 2) inversion break-up and 3) fanning. All three occur in connection with stable atmospheric conditions (generally characterized by temperature inversions).
